How This Manual Is Updated (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Policy revisions are issued by Supervisory Releases (SR), which contain a narrative describing the changes. Replacement manual pages are issued with the SR to internal DHHS holders of the paper version of the manual. The electronic version of the manual, available internally for DHHS as well as on the web, is centrally updated through the Version Control process.

The header of each page identifies:

• the Chapter, Part, or Section number and name;

• the manual affected (MAM);

• the SR number which released the policy;

• the effective date of the policy; and

• for those with access to the Department’s computer network, an automated link to Previous Policy, if applicable.

Part numbers are three digits; the first digit identifies the Chapter (e.g., Part 409 is from Chapter 400). Section numbers further divide the Parts and use the Part number followed by a decimal point and two digits (e.g., 409.01 refers to Chapter 400, Part 409, Section 01).

As this manual is the basis for administering and implementing DFA programs, it will be updated as policy is revised.

body:
113 APPLICATION PROCESSING TIME FRAMES (MAM)

SR-21-24 Dated 3/20 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

An application must be acted upon promptly and without undue delay. For the MAGI categories, non-MAGI categories where no medical determination is needed to determine eligibility, and non-MAGI re-applications that require a disability determination but a previous approval has a future review date or no review date, and the assistance group does not report having a trust or annuity, eligibility is determined using a simplified process that does not required an interactive interview. For all categories of medical assistance, generate a Notice of Decision (NOD) to the individual as soon as eligibility has been determined, but no later than:

• 45 calendar days from the application date for all MAGI-related medical assistance groups and for Old Age Assistance (OAA), Aid to the Needy Blind (ANB), Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) and SLMB135, and Qualified Disabled Working Individuals (QDWI); and

• 90 calendar days from the application date for Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD), Nursing Facility (NF) services, all Home and Community-Based Care (HCBC) services, including Choices for Independence (CFI) services, Medicaid for Employed Adults with Disabilities (MEAD), and Medicaid for Employed Older Adults with Disabilities (MOAD).

Exceptions:

• Generate the NOD to the individual as soon as possible when the decision cannot be reached due to a failure or delay on the part of the applicant or any other unusual circumstances beyond the control of DHHS. Document the reason for the delay in the case file.

• Generate the NOD to the individual as soon as possible when the individual is not eligible for medical assistance and the individual's information is being shared electronically with the Federally Facilitated Marketplace (FFM) for eligibility determination for one of the other Affordable Care Act (ACA)-related health coverage options.

References: 42 CFR 435.911, 42 CFR 435.912, 42 CFR 435.1200(e)

body:
115 JOINT APPLICATIONS (MAM)

SR 21-24 Dated 3/20 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

BFA Form 800, Application for Assistance

BFA Form 800, Application for Assistance, along with BFA Form 800 Insert, is used by financial assistance, medical assistance, child care, and Food SNAP applicants. However, if a current recipient applies for SNAP benefits or another program of assistance during the in-office redetermination interview for the other program, Form 800HR, HEIGHTS-generated Application for Assistance, may be used rather than a separate BFA Form 800/BFA Form Insert.

Determine the programs of assistance for which the individual wants to apply and conduct one interview for all programs; however, MAGI-related medical assistance groups and non-MAGI assistance groups with no trust or annuity and when no medical determination is needed to determine eligibility, and for non-MAGI re-applications that require a disability determination but a previous approval has a future review date or no review date , are not required to participate in an interview.

Exception: If necessary to meet the SNAP expedited processing time frames, finish the interview for the remaining programs at a later date.

When the same eligibility factors are involved in each program, verification provided to meet the verification requirements for one program of assistance is used to meet the verification requirements for all other programs of assistance requested. For example, if each program of assistance the individual has requested requires verification of citizenship and the individual provides a Birth Certificate, the Birth Certificate satisfies citizenship verification requirements for all the programs of assistance requested. However, each program has different eligibility policies which cannot be used for programs outside of the program for which the policy is written. For example, SNAP allows shelter deductions. The FANF program does not have these deductions. Therefore, shelter and utility costs may be subtracted from income that is considered available to the household only when determining SNAP eligibility and benefit allotment, and not when determining FANF eligibility and benefit allotment.

BFA Form 800MA, Application for Health Coverage & Help Paying Costs

BFA Form 800MA, Application for Health Coverage & Help Paying Costs, is used by Medical Assistance applicants only. BFA Form 800MA collects eligibility information specific to *Medical Assistance, Qualified Health Plans (QHPs), and Insurance Affordability Programs, including Advance Payments of the Premium Tax Credit (APTCs) and Cost-Sharing Reductions (CSRs).

BFA Form 800 *must be completed in addition to BFA Form 800MA when the individual would also like to apply for other forms of assistance, such as cash, SNAP benefits, and child care assistance. An interview is not required for MAGI medical assistance groups or for the non-MAGI medical assistance groups and services that do not have a medical determination, and for non-MAGI re-applications that require a disability determination but a previous approval has a future review date or no review date; interviews are required for, and requests for cash, SNAP, and child care assistance, and the non-MAGI medical assistance groups and services that require a medical determination or that have a trust or annuity.

Do not delay the eligibility decision in one program when all the required verification is provided for that program but not for the other(s).

Application processing time frames must be met for each program of assistance for which the individual applied. If individuals are denied for one program while a decision is pending for other programs, they are not required to file a new application. Use the original application to determine eligibility for the remaining programs.

References: He-W 601.01(n) & (p), He-W 601.03(a), He-W 602.03, RSA 167:8,I, 7 CFR 273.2(b)(3), 42 CFR 435.907, 42 CFR 435.911, 42 CFR 435.1200(e), 45 CFR 206:10(a)(1) & (b)(1)-(3)

127 PENDING INFORMATION (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

If more information or verification is needed to complete the application, allow the individual at least 10 calendar days to provide it. The due date must be a workday.

New HEIGHTS will generate the AE0026, Verification Checklist , which explains what information or verification is needed and the date the information or verification is due. The AE0026 is automatically generated anytime something is entered onto the Application Entry screen, marked "Not Yet Verified," and eligibility is run. If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use the paper backup DFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

If the individual does not provide the information or verification by the due date, deny the application on the due date.

Exceptions:

. If the eligibility factor in question does not affect the eligibility of the entire case, disqualify the ineligible member(s) and open the remaining members.

. If the assistance is being denied due to lack of verification and the individual provides all the required verification within 30 days of the date of the denial notice:

- have the individual fill out DFA Form 800, Application for Assistance , with their name, address, program of assistance, and signature;

- ensure that no other changes have occurred in the case that would affect eligibility and that no new program services have been requested on DFA Form 800 other than those which were originally denied; and

- if the individual continues to meet all program eligibility requirements, generate medical benefits in accordance with PART 121 , Initiation of Medical Assistance .

131 LENGTH OF ELIGIBILITY (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Medical assistance, QMB, QDWI, SLMB, or SLMB135 cases do not have certification periods. Cases remain eligible until they are determined ineligible.

Schedule redeterminations of eligibility at least every 12 months.

. The first redetermination date is set by counting 12 months from the month of application. The month of application is always zero.

. Assign subsequent redeterminations by counting 12 months from the date of the currently scheduled redetermination. The current redetermination month is always zero.

Review individuals more frequently when either of the following occurs:

. There is a change in case circumstances that affects other eligibility factors; or

. There is conflicting information regarding eligibility.

139 COMPLAINTS AND ADMINISTRATIVE APPEALS (MAM)

SR 13-19 Dated 09/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

If any individual or authorized representative expresses dissatisfaction with a decision regarding medical assistance benefits or services, take all of the following steps:

1. Explain the basis for the decision and the applicable policy requirements.

2. Provide the individual an opportunity to have a conference with the Supervisor.

3. Provide the individual an opportunity to request an administrative appeal. If requested within 15 days from the date on the notice of the action being appealed, the individual's medical assistance benefits may, under certain circumstances, be continued or reinstated at the previous level until the decision on the appeal is reached .

body:
143 ACTIONS ON CHANGES (MAM)

SR 15-03 Dated 01/15 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

All reported actions must be acted upon within 10 business days of the date the change is reported. Actions on changes vary depending upon the type of medical assistance (MA) received: Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) MA or non-MAGI MA.

MAGI M edical A ssistance

Because verification requirements differ for MAGI MA, when a change is reported during the eligibility period, do the following:

. record the reported change and the date.

. If a change is reported in residency, household composition, tax filing status, pregnancy, caretaker relative status, or application for other benefits, consider the reported information as verified and after entering the change, no further action is necessary.

. if a change is reported in earned income , do the following:

- if the earned income that i s reported by the recipient is within 10% of the verified amount currently associated with the case , or the difference in income exceeds 10% but the difference will not affect eligibility in any way, consider the reported information verified. Enter the change and require no further proof.

- if the earned income exceeds the 10% threshold and will affect eligibility, follow the steps below for when a change is reported in earned income for Non-MAGI MA.

. for all other types of changes that have occurred , notify the individual of any needed verification because of the reported change using New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance . If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use paper backup DFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance . Allow the individual 10 calendar days from the date the change occurs to provide any needed proof of the change. Exception : If a change is reported in unearned income, only request verification if the unearned exceeds the 10% threshold and eligibility will be effected.

Non-MAGI M edical A ssistance

When a change is reported in earned income , do the following :

. first attempt collateral contact. If collateral contact is successful, consider the reported information as verified and no further action is necessary.

. if collateral contact is unsuccessful, verify the reported change by using:

- information provided by the client, if the change is expected to decrease benefits. See PART 147 , CHANGES THAT DECREASE BENEFITS ; or

- standard verification procedures, if the change is expected to increase benefits. See PART 145 , CHANGES THAT INCREASE BENEFITS .

For other reported changes that have occurred associated with a non-MAGI MA case , take all of the following actions:

. Record the reported change and the date.

. Notify the individual of any needed verification because of the reported change, using New HEIGHTS-generated AE0055, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance . If New HEIGHTS is unavailable, use paper backup DFA Form 808, Proof Needed to Determine Your Assistance .

. Allow the individual 10 calendar days from the date the change occurs to provide verification of the change.

. Determine the effect of the change on the individual ' s eligibility and medical assistance benefits.

Exception : Schedule a redetermination appointment prior to the change if policy requires that assistance be terminated in the month in which the change takes place.

All Types of Assistance

For other reported changes that are expected to occur , take all of the following actions:

. Record the reported change and the date the change is expected to occur.

. Within 10 working days of the date the change was expected to occur, contact the individual to request verification of the change , if needed .

References : He-W 606.01, He-W 606.100, He-W 636.01(b), He-W 64 4.01(c), He-W 684.01(a)(5) , He-W 842.02, RSA 167:4-a, RSA 167:17, 42 CFR 435.945, 42 CFR 435.952, 42 CFR 435.956, 45 CFR 206.10(a)(9)

145 CHANGES THAT INCREASE BENEFITS (MAM)

SR 15-03 Dated 01/15 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

All changes must be acted upon as described in PART 143 , ACTIONS ON CHANGES . Note that when a change is reported in earned income that will increase medical assistance benefits for a non-MAGI case:

. first attempt collateral contact. If collateral contact is successful, consider the reported information as verified and no further action is necessary; or

. if collateral contact is unsuccessful, use standard verification procedures.

For changes that increase benefits for all categories of medical assistance, make the change effective for the 1 st of the next month if verification of the change is needed and is provided within time frames.

If verification is needed and is not provided within time frames, terminate the case.

If the individual provides verification within the advance notice period, make the change and make the change effective for the 1 st of the next month.

Restore lost medical assistance benefits if the individual reported the change and provided verification on time, but DHHS failed to make the change within the time frames specified above.

References : He-W 606.01, He-W 606.100, He-W 636.01(b), He-W 64 4.01(c), He-W 684.01(a)(5) , He-W 842.02, RSA 167:4-a, RSA 167:17, 42 CFR 435.945, 42 CFR 435.952, 42 CFR 435.956, 45 CFR 206.10(a)(9)

147 CHANGES THAT DECREASE BENEFITS (MAM)

SR 15-03 Dated 01/15 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

All changes must be acted upon as described in PART 143 , ACTIONS ON CHANGES . Note that when a change is reported in earned income that will reduce or terminate medical assistance benefits for a non-MAGI MA case:

. first attempt collateral contact. If collateral contact is successful, consider the reported information as verified and no further action is necessary; or

. if collateral contact is unsuccessful, verify the change using the information that the client provided. No additional paper verification is needed.

Exception : Standard verification procedures must be used for:

. changes in earned income discovered through the New Hire Match. Attempt collateral contact first but if it is unsuccessful, send DFA Form 756, Employment Verification , to the employer, and allow 10 days for the required verification; or

. insufficient or questionable client information which does not allow the FSS to verify the change based upon the client's statement.

For all other changes that will reduce or terminate medical assistance benefits for any category of medical assistance, take action as follows:

. Determine whether the change will decrease or terminate medical assistance benefits within 10 business days after the individual reports the change.

. Terminations are effective the last day of the ANP. Decreases in level of eligibility are effective the day after the ANP expires.

. If verification is needed and is not provided when the individual reports the change and you cannot determine if the result will be a decrease or termination, allow the individual 10 calendar days to provide verification of the change.

If verification is needed and is not provided within the time frames, terminate the case.

Process a claim if an overpayment or overissuance occurs.

References : He-W 606.01, He-W 606.100, He-W 636.01(b), He-W 64 4.01(c), He-W 684.01(a)(5) , He-W 842.02, RSA 167:4-a, RSA 167:17, 42 CFR 435.945, 42 CFR 435.952, 42 CFR 435.956, 45 CFR 206.10(a)(9)

SR 13-19 Dated 09/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

The state or federal government initiates mass changes that can affect all individuals or large numbers of individuals. Mass changes include the following:

. income eligibility standards;

. cost-of-living adjustments for Social Security, SSI, VA, and other federal benefits; or

. other eligibility criteria based on legislation or regulations.

When mass changes occur:

. eligibility or medical assistance benefits are adjusted automatically; and

. a Notice of Decision (NOD) is generated to notify individuals of the results of any changes.

If an individual requests an administrative appeal as a result of a decrease or termination in medical assistance benefits, and contacts the Department within 15 days on the NOD, reinstate medical assistance benefits to the pre-change level only if the issue contested is that:

. eligibility or the amount of medical assistance benefits was improperly computed; or

. a federal law or regulation was misapplied or misinterpreted.

151 ADDITION OF AN INDIVIDUAL (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Determine eligibility when a new individual must be added to the case.

Process a request to add a new individual as if it were a new application for that person. A new DFA Form 800, Application for Assistance , or DFA Form 800MA, Application for Health Coverage and Help Paying Costs , is not required.

Process the application within time frames, using the date of the request as the file date.

If the new individual is ineligible or does not provide enough information, take the steps in the following chart:

Reason for Ineligibility Action Refuses or fails to provide required verification for an individual who must be included in the assistance group Terminate entire case Refuses or fails to provide required verification for an individual who may be included in the assistance group Deny the new member only Required verification is not available for the new member Deny the new member only New member does not meet the program criteria for inclusion in the assistance group Deny the new member only

If the addition of a new individual is not reported within time frames, process a claim for overpayment if:

• the new individual must be included in the assistance group, and

• including the new individual would have decreased or terminated medical assistance benefits.

SR 14-17 Dated 09/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

A desk review is a review and verification of a reported or discovered change in an eligibility factor or individual circumstances and the resulting change to the case, if any.

Conduct a desk review when a change does not warrant a full redetermination of all eligibility factors. Conduct a full redetermination instead of a desk review if the individual requests one.

. Notify the individual of any required information or verification.

. Allow the individual 10 working days to provide the information or verification.

175.07 Youth Community Reentry (MAM)

SR 26-07 Dated 01/25 Previous Policy

_ ____________________________________________________________

Eligible juvenile is defined as a juvenile under age 21 or individual eligible for former foster care medical assistance who is post-adjudication. Eligible juveniles will receive limited Medicaid benefits 30 days prior to their release which includes:

· screening and diagnostic services 30 days prior to release (or within 1 week or as soon as practicable after release)

· targeted case management 30 days prior to release and for at least 30 days post release including reentry planning, resource navigation, and community-based provider care coordination; and

· 30-day supply of prescription medications upon release.

Individuals ages 18 through 20 or up to age 26 who meet former foster care eligibility may be eligible for both the limited benefits under the youth reentry and the adult reentry.

The eligible juvenile is eligible for the limited benefit whenever they are within 30 days of their expected release date.

201 GENERAL INFORMATION (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

When an individual requests medical assistance, determine whether the individual meets the requirements of any of the medical assistance programs administered by DHHS.

Medical assistance is available:

. under the adult program to individuals who are aged, blind, or physically or mentally disabled;

. under the MAGI-related categories: (Children's Medicaid [which includes Children with Severe Disabilities (CSD)], Expanded Children's Medicaid, Pregnant Women, Parents/Caretaker Relatives, Former Foster Care Child, and Family Planning Expansion Category;

. through the Medicaid for Employed Adults with Disabilities (MEAD) program ;

. through Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA) ;

. through the Home Care for Children with Severe Disabilities (HC-CSD) program ;

. through long-term care (LTC) services , which includes nursing facility (NF) and home and community-based care (HCBC) services ; and

. through the Medicare Savings Programs (MSP) (QMB, SLMB/SLMB135, QDWI) .

The following chart identifies the type of assistance provided by each program:

Programs Financial Assistance Medical Assistance Old Age Assistance (OAA) Yes Yes Aid to the Needy Blind (ANB) Yes Yes Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD) Yes Yes Medicaid for Employed Adults with Disabilities (MEAD) No Yes Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) No Limited Qualified Disabled and Working Individuals (QDWI) No Limited Specified Low-Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB) and SLMB135 No Limited Parents Caretaker Relative MA Yes Yes *Former Foster Care Child MA * *No Yes Children's Medicaid (CM) No Yes Expanded Children's Medicaid No Yes * Pregnant Women MA No Yes Family Planning Medical Assistance (FP MA ) No Limited Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA) Yes Yes

Individuals who meet the categorical requirements of either OAA, ANB, or APTD and who meet additional requirements relative to special living arrangements may be entitled to either a higher standard of need or expanded services.

Special Living Arrangements Financial Assistance Medical Assistance Residential Care Facility (RCF) Yes Yes Community Residence (including enhanced family care facilities) Yes Yes Nursing Facility (NF) No Yes Home and Community-Based Care for the Elderly and Chronically Ill (HCBC-ECI) Yes Yes Home and Community-Based Care for the Developmentally Disabled (HCBC-DD) Yes Yes Home and Community-Based Care for Individuals with an Acquired Brain Disorder (HCBC-ABD) Yes Yes Home and Community-Based Care for In-Home Support (HCBC-IHS) Yes Yes

203 CATEGORICAL REQUIREMENTS (MAM)

SR 15-03 Dated 01/15 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

An individual who requests medical assistance must be determined eligible according to certain criteria for that program. These criteria are referred to as the categorical requirements.

The individual must also meet general and financial requirements.

All these factors are then used to determine the individual's "level of eligibility," which means the type of medical assistance for which the individual may be eligible:

. categorically-needy medical assistance;

. medically-needy medical assistance; or

. in and out medically needy medical assistance.

Exception: Certain refugees who do not meet the categorical requirements for OAA, APTD, ANB, or FANF may be eligible for Refugee Cash Assistance (RCA) or Refugee Medical Assistance (RMA).

265 MEDICALLY-NEEDY MEDICAL ASSISTANCE (MAM)

SR 19-06 Dated 01/19 Previous Policy

_____________________________________________________________

Medically-needy medical assistance (MA) is a level of medical assistance provided to an individual who:

. meets the general, categorical, and technical requirements but not the financial requirements, for categorically-needy MA ; and

. meets the finan cial requirements for medically-needy medical assistance.

Although there are some exceptions, in general, use the following when determining the financial eligibility of an individual for medically-needy medical assistance:

. the protected income level (PI L) when determining income eligibility for med ically-needy medical assistance; and

. a special medically-needy resource limit .

Each program of assistance will specify its medically-needy financial requirements, and the different income or resource limits if applicable, if medically-needy medical assistance is offered.

In and Out MA is a type of medically-needy MA. This category of assistance is offered when an individual's countable income exceeds the medically-needy MA income limit. See PART 625 , IN AND OUT MEDICAL ASSISTANCE , for more information.

Not every category of categorically-needy MA offers a corresponding medically-needy MA category. Medically-Needy MA or In and Out MA is not offered for:

. Medicaid for Empl oyed Adults with Disabilities (MEAD);

. the Medicare Savings Programs (MSP) [ Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB & SLMB135), and Qualified Disabled and Working Individual (QDWI) programs ];

. Former Foster C are Child MA;

. Family Planning MA; or

. Granite Advantage Health Care Program (Granite Advantage) .

body:
313 ASSIGNMENT OF CHILD/SPOUSAL MEDICAL SUPPORT RIGHTS (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

_______________________________________________________________

Applications for Medical Assistance on Behalf of Parents and Other Adults and Their Children

If parents or other adults apply for Medicaid on behalf of themselves and their children, the applicant must assign medical support and payment rights to DHHS and cooperate in establishing paternity, obtaining medical support and payments, and providing information about liable third parties as a condition of their own eligibility, unless they are exempt. Pregnant women eligible for MCPW are exempt. Parents who are not exempt from the requirement have an ongoing obligation to cooperate in order to maintain their eligibility for Medicaid. The decision whether or not to cooperate will not affect their child's eligibility for Medicaid.

Cooperation with this requirement includes fully completing Division of Child Support (DCSS) Form 725, Application for Child Support Services , to initiate assignment.

If an applicant indicates an absent parent is "unknown," the individual must meet with a DCSS representative as a condition of eligibility.

Medical assistance applicants who refuse to assign support, complete the DCSS Form 725, or meet with a DCSS representative as required, are denied assistance. No good cause exists. Document the refusal in the record.

The support that must be assigned to DHHS includes payments which are owed, are pending, or are continuing as of the date the applicant assigns rights to support income to DHHS.

Child-Only Applications

If a parent or caretaker relative files an application for Medicaid on behalf of a child only, the requirements to assign the child's rights to support and payment and cooperate in establishing paternity and pursuing medical support payment do not apply to the parent or caretaker relative. It is not a condition of the child's eligibility that the parent or caretaker relative assign the child's rights to support and payment and cooperate in establishing paternity and pursuing medical support payment.

Although the parent or caretaker is not required to assign the child's rights over to DHHS, the automatic assignment of an individual's rights to payment for medical care by third parties to the extent that Medicaid has made a payment is required. Receipt of medical assistance is an assignment to DHHS of the parent or caretaker relative's rights to all third party medical insurance or payments.

Although parents and caretaker relatives are not required to cooperate in establishing paternity and pursing medical support when only the child is applying for Medicaid, FSS must ask the parent or caretaker relative whether the child has health insurance to identify legally liable third party resources.

References: RSA 161:C-22, RSA 161-H:1 et seq, 42 CFR 435.610, 42 U.S.C. 1396a, 42 USC 1396K, 42 USC 1396r-6(a)(25)(H)

401 GENERAL INFORMATION (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

In addition to categorical and general requirements, an assistance group must meet financial eligibility requirements to receive assistance. Financial requirements are broken into two components:

. resources, and

. income. See Chapter 500 , Income .

An assistance group which meets the income requirements is income-eligible. An assistance group which meets the resource requirements is resource-eligible. The assistance group is considered financially eligible if both income and resource requirements are met. Chapter 600 , Standards and Budgets , explains income limits and budgeting procedures for the various programs and coverage groups.

403 WHOSE RESOURCES COUNT? (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

There is no resource test for MAGI-related medical assistance; resources do not count in the MAGI eligibility determination process.

For the non-MAGI-related medical assistance groups, consider all resources owned by or available to all members of the assistance group. Assistance group composition differs based on the type of assistance requested. See Chapter 200 , Program Criteria , to determine who is included in the assistance group.

Resources may be counted from people not in the assistance group, such as alien sponsors and excluded parents.

Exception: If an institutionalized individual has a community spouse, consider the resources of both the institutionalized individual and the spouse, even though they do not reside together at initial eligibility determination only. See PART 417 , Resource Assessment . and PART 419 , Protection of Resources .

References: He-W 856.04, 42 CFR 435.603

body:
405 TREATMENT OF RESOURCES (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Resources are either excluded or countable depending on the type of assistance requested. Count the equity value of all countable resources unless otherwise specified.

If the individual has combined excluded resources with countable resources, the individual must verify the portion that is excludable. Encourage the individual to retain excluded resources separately from countable resources.

Accumulated interest, changes in equity value of life insurance policies, and changes in the value of stocks and bonds do not have to be reported between redeterminations.

Individuals already receiving benefits may reduce resources which are in excess of the program limit, if all the criteria below are met:

• The individual’s resources include personal property assets which cannot be readily converted to cash. Examples include vehicles, aboveground swimming pools, art objects, and investment antiques.

• The individual must report excess resources in a timely manner.

• The individual must reduce their resources to program limits no later than the month following the month in which resources first exceeded the limit. During this time period, the individual must prove to the District Office Supervisor that the individual is making a good faith effort to sell the personal property resource which caused the individual to exceed the resource limit. If the individual fails to reduce resources to allowable limits within this time period, terminate assistance for the entire assistance group.

References: He-W 856.04; RSA 167:17

body:
409 VERIFICATION (MAM)

SR 26-08 Dated 03/26 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Verification of Resources

The Department accepts self-attestation of resources at initial application. Resources held in financial institutions are verified primarily through the Asset Verification System (AVS) based upon self-attestation and/or what the individual has provided for resources during the eligibility determination process. If the AVS returns all account information, no further documentation is required.

Proof of resources is only required to maintain eligibility if:

· there is a discrepancy between what the individual reported and the AVS (see 410 REASONABLE COMPATIBILITY FOR RESOURCES MAM ); or

· there is a reported resource that cannot be verified with the AVS.

Document the countable or excluded status of all the assistance group's resources. Document and list the value of countable resources. Show computations for determining equity or values for those resources with allowable deductions. Total the value of countable resources to prove the assistance group (AG) is within the appropriate resource limit.

Proof of resources may also be required to maintain eligibility for all countable and excluded resources, that cannot be verified electronically , at the initial eligibility determination and subsequent redetermination when: · a change is reported or discovered; or · conflicting information is discovered.

Reasonable explanation may be an acceptable verification if the attestation and information received from the data source are inconsistent.

Deny or terminate assistance for the entire assistance group if the individual refuses or fails to verify resources.

Asset Verification System (AVS) Requests

For non-MAGI categories of medical assistance, the AVS is used to verify the self-attested resources and to conduct a random search for undisclosed resources owned by the assistance group (AG). The AVS will detect and verify most common checking and savings accounts held in financial institutions.

AVS requests will be automatically sent out at: · initial eligibility determination; and · subsequent redeterminations. If the AVS response indicates the individuals’ resources (disclosed and/or undisclosed) are within the appropriate resource limit, and are reasonably compatible, the AVS responses are adequate verification of the AG resources, and no further documentation is required. Manually request AVS verification or reasonable explanation of an individual’s resources when: · a change is reported or discovered; · conflicting information is discovered; · the individual did not disclose all the resources contained in the AVS response; · the individual has more resources than the appropriate resource limit; or · the information is not reasonably compatible at initial application.

The request for additional information or documentation must be limited to the specific resource(s) with conflicting information.

The AVS responses of electronic information verifying an individual’s resources will be available within 15 days of the AVS request.

Transfer of Assets

LTC Workers will use AVS responses to examine whether an applicant for NF or HCBS made an impermissible transfer. An impermissible transfer occurs when both of the following factors are present:

· An asset is transferred for less than fair market value; and

· The asset is transferred for the purpose of gaining LTC Medicaid eligibility.

The AVS provides monthly balances on all accounts as of the first of each month for the 60 months prior to the application. LTC workers will review the account balances and determine if there are any impermissible transfers based on the balances each month. For any transfers that appear potentially impermissible, staff may, if appropriate , accept a reasonable explanation and self-attestation from the applicant before requesting paper documentation or third-party verification.

If the AVS does not return an account, request paper documentation as follows:

· Monthly statements for the 12 months immediately preceding the month the application was submitted; and

· One monthly statement for each of the 4 years preceding the 12 months.

NOTE: Statements must be from the same month each year and be the same month preceding the date of application.

Note: AVS will not do a lookback for trusts if the trust has a separate Employer Identification Number (EIN).

R eferences : He-W 856.01; He-W 856.06; 42 CFR § 435.949; 42 CFR § 435.952

410 REASONABLE COMPATIBILITY OF RESOURCES (MAM)

SR 26-08 Dated 03/26 Previous Policy

_ ____________________________________________________________

Reasonable Compatibility

Reasonable Compatibility refers to the standard used to compare the self-attested resources and the resources reported by an electronic data source. Reasonable Compatibility applies to all non-MAGI Categories of Medical Assistance (MA) recipients at initial application .

Note : resources are not countable for MAGI-Categories of medical assistance .

Reasonable Compatibility standard for Resources at Initial Application :

v Reasonable compatibility of resources DOES NOT apply at Redetermination.

v Applicable for non-MAGI cases only.

At initial application, the self-attested resources are compared to the electronic data source (Asset Verification System - AVS), and are managed as follows:

v When the combined value of the self-attested resources is at/below the resource limit and the electronic data source (AVS) reported resources, and any other countable resources reported are under the resource limit , the information is reasonably compatible, and the resource test is met. No verifications are required.

v When the combined value of the self-attested resources is at/below the resource limit and the electronic data source (AVS) reported resources, and any other countable resources reported are over the resource limit , if the difference is within 10%, the information is reasonably compatible, and the resource test is met. No verifications are required.

v When the combined value of the self-attested resources is at/below the resource limit and the electronic data source (AVS) reported resources, and any other countable resources reported are over the resource limit, if the difference is greater than 10%, the information is not reasonably compatible, and the resource test is not met. The self-attested resources are used to open the medical and verification of resources are required.

v When the combined value of the self-attested resources is at/below the resource limit and the electronic data source (AVS) reported no resource results , the information is not reasonably compatible, and the resource test is not met. The self-attested resources are used to open the medical and verification of resources are required.

Please see the scenarios below, based on a $2,500 resource limit ($2,750 with the 10% standard applied) for specific examples:

Scenario Client Attestation AVS Result Reasonable compatible Outcome Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and the AVS matches what was self-attested $2,000 at Bank A $2,000 at Bank A Yes Combined total is under $2750 No further information needed Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and the AVS reports resources above the resource limit , and the difference is less than 10% $2450 at Bank A $2505 at Bank A Yes Combined total is under $2750 No further information needed Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and the AVS reports an unreported bank account , with the total combined resources below the resource limit $2,000 at Bank A $2,000 at Bank A $200 at Bank B ($2,200 combined total between Bank A and B) Yes Combined total is under $2750 No further information needed Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and the AVS reports an unreported bank account, with the total combined resources over the resource limit and greater than 10% $2,000 at Bank A $2,000 at Bank A $2,000 at Bank B ($4,000 combined total between Bank A and B) No Combined total is over $2750 Open medical with self-attested resources and request additional verification DX0019 Asset Verification Request is generated and EC is set Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and no information was returned by the AVS $2,000 at Bank A No bank information found No Open medical with self-attested resources and request additional verification DX0019 Asset Verification Request is generated and EC is set. Client self-attested to resources below the resource limit and the AVS reports resources above the resource limit, and the difference is greater than 10% $2,000 at Bank A $3,500 at Bank A No Combined total is over $2750 Open medical with self-attested resources and request additional verification DX0019 Asset Verification Request is generated and EC is set

body:
503 AVAILABLE AND ANTICIPATED INCOME (MAM)

SR 25-07 Dated 02/25 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Income (earned or unearned) is considered available when an assistance group member receives it on a regular and recurring basis. Regular and recurring means an income amount that the assistance group can reasonably anticipate for use each month. However, some income is not received by the assistance group, yet is considered available to the assistance group anyway. See Deemed Income . For income that is infrequent see Irregular Income .

Anticipated income is considered available when its receipt is reasonably certain, and the income is intended to continue in the future. These cases are handled on a case-by-case basis.

Income that represents contributions, panhandling, or compensation for a period of more than 1 month, or varies steadily from month to month, is averaged to obtain a monthly figure. The monthly average is then considered to be the available income the individual is expected to have for their use each month.

Example: During an initial interview for an application dated 4/25/2024, Tanya stated she is meeting her phone bill expense by panhandling once a week. She states she started panhandling in March 2024 and intends to continue through her certification period. Tanya provides the following verifications of her panhandling income for March:

-3/7/2024: $55

-3/14/2024: $32

-3/21/24: $74

-3/28/2024: $91

Because this income is considered available and anticipated to continue, this would be countable income. The monthly average unearned income would be $272.79. ($55+$32+$74+91=$252/4 (weeks)=$63 weekly average X4.33= $272.79).

References : He-W 852.06; RSA 161:4-a, IX, RSA 167:3-c, I; RSA 167:4; RSA 167:7, IV; 42 U.S. Code § 1382a

.

505 WHOSE INCOME COUNTS? (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

What income counts is based upon whether the person is applying for or receiving modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-related medical assistance or non-MAGI-related medical assistance. Consider the available income of all members of the assistance group when determining eligibility. Income is always considered to belong to the individual on whose behalf it is paid e.g., child support or SSA paid on behalf of a child is considered that child's income. Assistance group composition differs based on the type of assistance requested. See Chapter 200 , Program Criteria , to determine who is included in the assistance group.

Some income is counted even if a person (such as a disqualified parent) is not part of the assistance group.

References: 42 CFR 435.603

507 TREATMENT OF INCOME (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

All income is considered either:

. excluded; or

. countable.

Excluded income of an assistance group member is not counted when determining eligibility.

Countable income is considered either:

. earned; or

. unearned.

There are allowable deductions and a standard disregard that are deducted from both earned and unearned income. Earned income is separated from unearned income due to additional disregards which are allowed for earned income only. See Chapter 600 , Standards and Budgets , for policy regarding disregards, deductions, and budgeting.

510 REASONABLE COMPATIBILITY STANDARD FOR INCOME (MAM)

SR 25-41 Dated 01/26 Previous Policy

_ ____________________________________________________________

Reasonable Compatibility

Reasonable Compatibility refers to the standard used to compare the self-attested income and income reported by an electronic data source. Reasonable Compatibility standard for income applies to all Medical Assistance (MA) recipients at initial application .

Reasonable Compatibility Standard for Income, at Initial Application .

v Reasonable compatibility of income DOES NOT apply at Redetermination.

At initial application the self-attested income is compared to the electronic data source (e.g. VCI/NHES), and is managed as follows:

Income (MAGI and non-MAGI cases)

· When the combined value of the self-attested income is at/below the income limit and the electronic data source (VCI) reported income, and any other countable income are under the income limit , the information is reasonably compatible, and the income test is met. No verifications are required.

· When the combined value of the self-attested income is at/below the income limit and the electronic data source (VCI) reported income, and any other countable income are over the income limit , if the difference between the two is within 10% , the information is reasonably compatible, and the income test is met. No verification of income is required.

· When the combined value of the self-attested income is at/below the income limit and the electronic data source (VCI) reported income, and any other countable income are over the income limit , if the difference between the two is greater than 10%, the information is not reasonably compatible, and the income test is not met. The self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is required.

· When the combined value of the self-attested income is at/below the income limit and the electronic data source (VCI) reported current employment but $0 income results , the information is not reasonably compatible, and the income test is not met. The self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is required.

· When the combined value of the self-attested income is at/below the income limit and the electronic data source (VCI) reported no results , The system will check NHES as a second data source, and if there is still no response the information is not reasonably compatible, and the income test is not met. The self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is required.

Scenario Compatibility Outcome Verification Required Self-attested income is at/below the income limit; electronic data source (VCI) reported income is below the income limit or all accountable income combined is below the limit. Reasonably compatible and the income test is met. No Self-attested income is at/below the income limit; electronic data source (VCI) reported income is over the income limit; difference between the two is at or less than 10% Reasonably compatible and the income test is met. No Self-attested income is at/below the income limit; electronic data source (VCI) reported income is over the income limit; difference between the two is greater than 10% Not reasonably compatible and the income test is not met. Yes, the self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is requested. Self-attested income is at/below the income limit; electronic data source (VCI) reported no response . The system will check NHES as a 2 nd data source if there is still no response. Not reasonably compatible and the income test is not met. Yes, the self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is requested. Self-attested income is at/below the income limit; electronic data source (VCI) reported current employment but $0 income results . Not reasonably compatible and the income test is not met. Yes, the self-attested income is used to open the medical and verification of income is requested.

v Children and pregnant women who have been determined eligible for medical assistance based on attested information at initial determination, are entitled to a 12-month Continuous Eligibility (CE) period. The department must not terminate coverage for individuals during a CE period if financial information obtained indicated the individual is not eligible. They must remain open for coverage through the end of the 12-month period following the effective date of eligibility based on the initial determination.

References : CFR § 435.952

609 CONVERSION TO MONTHLY AMOUNTS (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Convert income, disregards, and deductions that are not received or paid monthly to a monthly amount. Use one of the following methods:

. multiply weekly amounts by 4.33;

. multiply biweekly amounts by 2.17;

. multiply semimonthly amounts by 2; or

. average amounts received for a period of more than one month e.g., divide yearly income by 12.

body:
613 COMPUTING ELIGIBILITY (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

To determine income eligibility for medical assistance in the upcoming sections, you may need to refer to the following parts of this manual:

. Chapter 200 , Program Criteria - This chapter describes household composition (who is included in the assistance group), the different programs, and living arrangements.

. Chapter 500 , Income - - This chapter describes the types of income and the appropriate treatments (excluded vs. countable and earned vs. unearned).

. Chapter 600 , Standards and Budgets - Refer to the following sections:

- 601 , Income Limits ;

- 603.01 , Earned Income Disregard (EID) ;

- 603.03 , Employment Expense Disregard (EED) ;

- 603.05 , Adult Standard Disregard ; and

- 605 , Deductions .

The computation of income varies according to the category of assistance requested and living arrangement. Use the following chart to determine which section describes the budgeting procedure for the specific type of assistance requested and living arrangement.

615 BUDGETING: Independent Living, RCF, CR, QMB, QDWI, SLMB and SLMB135 (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Use the following steps to compute income for assistance groups requesting or residing in:

. independent living,

. residential care facility,

. community residence, and

. QMB, QDWI, SLMB, and SLMB135.

1. Subtract the earned income disregard from individual or combined gross earned income in accordance with Section 603.01 , Earned Income Disregard , to obtain net income

2. Add the countable gross unearned income for each individual in the assistance group to the total net earned income calculated in Step 1.

Exception: Do not count the current year's January cost of living (COLA) increase as unearned income until April 1 for QMB, QDWI, SLMB, and SLMB135 cases who request assistance for January, February or March.

3. Subtract the adult standard disregard.

4. Subtract any allowable deductions. The result is the case net income.

5. Compare net income to the appropriate income limit.

If the net income exceeds the appropriate income limit for... Then... . Independent Living . Residential Care Facility . Community Residence . Determine potential In and Out eligibility. See Part 625 , In and Out Medical Assistance ; or . Determine potential eligibility for MEAD. See Part 211 , MEDICAID FOR EMPLOYED ADULTS WITH DISABILITIES.

617 BUDGETING: MAGI (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

When computing income for assistance groups requesting the MAGI categories of medical assistance, first determine who is included in the household composition of each member of the assistance group in accordance with PART 259 , COMPOSTION OF MAGI ASSISTANCE GROUPS . Each member of the assistance group may have a different household composition and household size. Who is included in each member's household composition determines whose income will count towards that member's income eligibility. The number of members in each individual's household composition determines the member's household size and income limit.

Once each individual's household composition is determined, u se the following steps to compute income separately for each individual in the assistance group:

1. Add the countable gross earned income and unearned income for each member of the individual's household composition.

2. Subtract any allowable deductions from individual 's combined countable gross earned income and unearned income in accordance with PART 605 , DEDUCTIONS , to obtain total net inc ome.

3 . Compare each individual's total net income to the appropriate income limit for each individual's household size .

If the individual's total net income exceeds the appropriate income limit, then determine potential In and Out eligibility. See PART 625 , In and Out Medical Assistance .

633 RECOUPMENT OF MEDICAL ASSISTANCE (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Medical assistance that is incorrectly paid on behalf of an individual is subject to recoupment if the erroneous payment was due to the client:

. withholding information;

. failing to comply with eligibility requirements; or

. making any type of error that results in incorrectly paid benefits.

Refer erroneously paid medical assistance cases that are caused by the above circumstances to the Office of Special Investigations (OSI).

Refer erroneously paid medical assistance cases involving nursing homes or Medicaid provider fraud to the Attorney General's Office.

See PART 635 , RECOUPMENT: LEGAL ACTION , for more information.

635 RECOUPMENT: LEGAL ACTION (MAM)

SR 13-36 Dated 11/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

The Attorney General’s Office is responsible for keeping the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) informed about court decisions in which DHHS has an interest.

If criminal proceedings are brought against the individual and a guilty verdict is rendered:

• follow the court order on the method and schedule of repayment; or

• pursue recoupment of medical assistance if the individual is fined and/or imprisoned and no repayment is ordered by the court. Failure of the court to order repayment does not prevent DHHS from pursuing recoupment action on its own, unless expressly prohibited by court order.

If criminal proceedings are brought against the individual and a not guilty verdict rendered, pursue recoupment of financial assistance. A court finding of innocence does not erase the existence of the overpayment.

See PART 633 , RECOUPMENT OF MEDICAL ASSISTANCE , for more information.

See the Adult Assistance Manual PART 631 , Recoupment of Financial Assistance , for additional information about financial assistance.

body:
Glossary A-words (MAM)

SR 26-07 Dated 01/25 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Adjudication - the court process that determines if an individual committed the act for which they are charged.

Administrative Error - An action or lack of action by BFA resulting in the underpayment or overpayment of an individual's level of benefit or resulting in an incorrect determination of eligibility or ineligibility.

Alien - A foreign-born person who has not been naturalized and is still a citizen of a foreign country; any individual who is not a citizen of the U.S.

Alien Sponsor - Any individual who executed an affidavit of support or similar agreement on behalf of an alien (who is neither the child of the sponsor nor the sponsor's spouse) as a condition of the alien's entry into the U.S. When deeming the sponsor's income, "sponsor" refers only to individuals and does not apply to churches, agencies, or organizations.

Alimony - Payments for maintenance and care made to and on behalf of former or estranged spouse.

Allowable Deduction - The amount subtracted from an income which represents an expense that has been made or must be made by an assistance group member or an individual whose income is counted when determining eligibility.

Alternate Payee Organization - Any organization that provides guardian, conservator, protective payee, authorized representative, or power of attorney services to NH citizens and receives Department of Health and Human Services benefits or notices on behalf of the individual.

Annuity - Any instrument which gives the right to receive fixed, periodic payments, either for life or a term of years.

Anticipated Change - A change that is expected to occur in the future.

Application - A formal request for assistance signed and dated by the applicant. BFA Form 800, Application for Assistance , is used to apply for most BFA programs. BFA Form 800MA, Application for Health Coverage & Help Paying Costs , is used to apply for Medicaid.

Assets - All income and resources of an individual and the individual's spouse, if married. Assets include income or resources to which the individual or spouse is entitled but does not receive because of any action by the individual or spouse, or person, including a court or administrative body, with legal authority to act in place of or on behalf of the individual or spouse or any person, including a court or administrative body, acting at the direction or upon the request of the individual or spouse.

Assignment of Rights to Support - A process whereby the right to receive and collect an individual's support is transferred to DHHS for the purpose of reimbursing CHIP medical assistance.

Assistance Group - The individuals living together, with or without benefit of a dwelling, whose needs, income, and resources, if resources are counted, are considered and combined together when determining eligibility and the amount of medical assistance.

Authorized Representative (AR ) - An individual who acts on behalf of the casehead in some or all aspects of initial and continuing eligibility. The AR may be anyone designated by the casehead or an individual acting responsibly on behalf of the casehead.

Available Income - All income considered to be regular and recurring or which is considered to be available for use regardless of actual receipt.

____________________________________________________________

Beneficiary - Any individual or individuals, designated in a trust instrument as benefitting in some way from the trust.

Boarder - An individual residing with others and paying reasonable compensation for lodging and meals.

Budgetary Unit - The group of individuals who are residing in the same housing unit whose needs are taken into account and whose income and resources, if resources are counted, may be used to determine eligibility for Medical Assistance.

Burial contract - A written agreement made between an individual and a business engaged in providing funeral services in which a portion of the individual's money has been set aside to pay for funeral expenses or burial.

Burial fund - A burial contract, burial trust, burial arrangement, or any other separately identifiable fund that has been clearly designated for burial expenses and is accessible.

Glossary C-words (MAM)

SR 26-07 Dated 01/25 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

CAP - The gross income eligibility limit for categorically needy medical assistance for the following types of cases: nursing facility, HCBC-CFI, and HCBC-DD.

Carceral Setting – a correctional facility, such as NH Dept of Corrections, county facilities, or youth correctional facilities.

Caretaker Relative - A specified relative who is not the biological, step, or adoptive parent, but is providing care for the children in the assistance group.

Case Income - The combined countable earned and unearned income of all assistance group members.

Cash Surrender Value - The amount of money which the owner of a life insurance policy would receive if the policy were cashed in.

Child Support - Payments for the maintenance and care made to and on behalf of a child.

Citizen - A person who, by birth, marriage, or naturalization, owes allegiance to a country, shares the political rights of that country, and is entitled to reciprocal protection from that country's government. Form purposes of this manual, citizen means U.S. citizen.

Client Error - A misunderstanding which results in the individual receiving an incorrect level of assistance.

COLA - The annual cost-of-living adjustment determined by the Social Security Administration (SSA).

Community Spouse - The non-institutionalized spouse of an institutionalized individual.

Community Reentry - a limited set of Medicaid benefits provided to individuals transitioning from incarceration back into the community.

Countable Income - Any type of income that is not excluded and which is used to determine eligibility or the amount of assistance.

Countable Resources - Real or personal property that is considered in determining eligibility, when resources are counted for a category of assistance.

Current Change - A change that has already occurred.

Glossary D-words (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Deduction - The amount subtracted from case income which represents an expense that has been made or must be made by an assistance group member or an individual whose income is counted when determining eligibility. Also known as an allowable deduction.

Deemed Income - income considered to be available for use regardless of actual receipt.

Deemed Individual Retirement Account under a Qualified Employer Plan - A separate account or annuity existing under an employer's established plan, which allows employees to make voluntary contributions. Established plans that meet the following criteria are considered a qualified employer plan:

- An employer-provided pension, profit-sharing, or stock/bond bonus plan created for the exclusive benefit of employees or their beneficiaries;

- A qualified employee annuity plan purchased by an employer for the benefit of the employee;

- An annuity plan provided by a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization, a public school, or created for the -benefit of self-employed ministers; or

- A deferred compensation plan (457b) maintained by a state, a political subdivision of a state, or an agency or instrumentality of a state or political subdivision of a state.

Disabled person - An individual who is prevented from working because of physical or mental impairment, disease, vision loss, or a combination of these conditions.

Disregard - An amount subtracted from individual or case income which is retained by the individual and is not counted in the determination of eligibility or the amount of assistance.

Dwelling - A housing unit that:

. is an individual ' s principal residence;

. has its own living facilities, including provisions for sleeping, eating, and sanitation; and

. has one postal address.

body:
Glossary E-words (MAM)

SR 26-07 Dated 01/25 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Earned Income — Cash or in-kind benefits received as payment for work performed either as an employee, through the receipt of wages, salaries, tips, or commissions, or as a self-employed individual.

Earned Income Disregard (EID) — An amount which is computed and subtracted from earned income, when an EID is allowed.

Elderly person — An individual who will be age 60 or older as of the last day of the month.

Eligible Juvenile - an individual who is under 21 years of age who was determined eligible for any medical assistance eligibility group, or an individual determined eligible for the mandatory eligibility group for former foster care children, immediately before becoming an inmate or while an inmate.

Employment Expense Disregard (EED) - A flat monthly rate set by policy or the actual expenses which are attributable to the earning of income, when an EED is allowed. The EED is subtracted from earned income.

Employment-Related Disregards — All disregards which are subtracted only from earned income, when these disregards are allowed. These include the employment expense disregard, the child/dependent care disregard, and the earned income disregard.

Equity Value — The amount of money that would be available to the owner after the sale of a resource. Determine the equity value by subtracting any encumbrances, such as the principal owed on a loan or mortgage, from the fair market value. Equity value of life insurance policies means the cash surrender value minus any encumbrances.

Excluded Income — Specific types of income which are not counted in the determination of eligibility or the amount of assistance.

Excluded Resource — Real or personal property that is not counted in determining eligibility, when resources are counted in the eligibility process for a category of assistance.

Fair Market Value — For all assets other than automobiles and trucks, means the price at which a willing seller and a willing buyer will trade. For automobiles and trucks, this means the "trade-in value" as specified in the National Automobile Dealers Association (N.A.D.A) Official Used Car Guide, also known as the "Blue Book."

Family — Children and parents who have a biological, foster, step- or adoptive relationship, and who reside in the same dwelling.

Fleeing Felon — Individuals who are fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody for a crime, or an attempt to commit a crime, that would be classified as a felony (or in the State of New Jersey, a high misdemeanor).

Grantor - Any individual who creates a trust, such as the individual, the individual's spouse, a person including a court or administrative body with legal authority to act in place of, or on behalf of, the individual or the individual's spouse; or a person, including a court or administrative body, acting at the direction or upon the request of the individual or the individual's spouse.

Gross Earned Income ( employed by another ) - The total amount of wages, salaries, tips, commissions, or the dollar value of in-kind benefits received by an employee as compensation for work performed before any payroll deductions are subtracted.

Gross Earned Income (self-employed) - The total amount of cash or the dollar value of in-kind benefits, minus the cost of doing business, which is received as compensation for work performed.

Gross Income - The total amount of cash or in-kind benefits, the total amount of earned income, the total self-employed income, and the total unearned income before deductions.

Gross Monthly Income - The total amount of money received by a family in one month before subtracting any expenses.

Glossary M-words (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Medicare Savings Program (MSP) — The umbrella term used to refer to the following medical assistance programs as a group: Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB), Specified Low Income Medicare Beneficiary (SLMB & SLMB135), and Qualified Disabled and Working Individual (QDWI) programs.

Minor Parent — an individual under age 18 who has a dependent child.

Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) — MAGI is a method for determining how income is counted, whose income is counted (the budget group), and the income limit based on the size of the budget group, for certain categories of medical assistance .

Month of application — The month in which the completed and signed application is received by the Department.

Glossary N-words (MAM)

SR 14-04 Dated 01/14 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Net Earned Income - An individual ' s monthly gross earned income minus all allowable employment-related disregards, if disregards are allowed. Also known as net monthly earned income .

Net Income - Gross income minus all allowable income disregards and deductions.

Non-Filer - For the MAGI categories of medical assistance, this means a person who does not expect or intend to file a federal tax return and 1) does not expect to be claimed by a tax dependent by someone else, or 2) does not have a tax household, or 3) is a tax dependent who falls under one of the 3 tax dependent exceptions .

Nonliquid Asset - A resource which cannot be readily converted to cash, such as vehicles, buildings, or land.

Nonprofit Agency - An organization that Internal Revenue Service has determined to be tax-exempt.

Notice of decision (NOD) - A computer-generated or manually prepared form which advises individuals of the results of eligibility determinations, changes in the amount of assistance or level of eligibility, and any other changes required by policy.

Glossary P-words (MAM)

SR 23-28 Dated 08/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Parent - A biological, adoptive, or stepparent, or an individual acting in the place of a parent, such as a foster parent or legal guardian.

Parental Support or Care - Financial support, guidance, physical care, and supervision of a dependent child.

Parolee - An alien admitted to the U.S. at the discretion of the U.S. Attorney General for emergency reasons in the public interest.

Penalty Date - The first date upon which a penalty for transfer of assets for less than fair market value can be assessed.

Penalty Period - The length of time during which payment for institutionalized medical services is denied.

Personal Interview - A conference between the individual or an authorized representative and the Family Services Specialist (FSS).

Personal Property - A form of cash or an item which can readily be converted to cash, i.e., liquid asset.

Private Institution - A facility which provides shelter, custody, or care to two or more persons and is managed entirely or partially by private funds.

Probation and Parole Violators - Individuals who are violating a condition of probation or parole under Federal or State law .

Proof - Documentation or information that establishes the accuracy of statements made by the individual.

Processing Month - The month in which computer entries are made and confirmed.

Protected Income Level ( PIL, medically needy medical assistance ) - The income limit that net income is compared to when determining eligibility for an assistance group that is not categorically eligible, such as In and Out Medical Assistance. The PIL is based on assistance group size.

Provided Shelter - Shelter that is provided at no charge to the assistance group.

Pure SSI Household - A household in which all members are SSI recipients.

Public Institution - A facility which affords shelter, custody, or care to two or more persons and is managed entirely or partially by any public instrumentality, official, or employee acting in an official capacity.

body:
Glossary Q-words (MAM)

SR 23-16 Dated 03/23 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Qualified Disability Expenses (QDE) — an expense related to the designated beneficiary as a result of living with their own blindness or disabilities. QDEs can include basic living expenses, food, education, housing, transportation, employment training and support, assistive technology and personal support services, health, prevention and wellness, financial management and administrative services, legal fees, expenses for oversight and monitoring, funeral and burial expenses, and other quality of life expenses.

Qualified Health Plan — Under the Affordable Care Act (ACA), a Qualified Health Plan is an insurance plan that is certified by the Federally Facilitated Marketplace (FFM), provides essential health benefits, follows established limits on cost-sharing (like deductibles, copayments, and out-of-pocket maximum amounts), and meets other requirements. A qualified health plan will have a certification from the FFM where it is sold.

Questionable — A statement made by an individual which is inconsistent with other statements made by the individual, inconsistent with information provided for current or past requests for assistance, or inconsistent with information received by the department from other sources.

body:
Glossary R-words (MAM)

SR 13-35 Dated 10/13 Previous Policy

____________________________________________________________

Real Property - Resources which are in the form of real estate, such as land or buildings.

Recoupment - The collection or recovery by DHHS of the value of assistance erroneously paid to an individual.

Refugee - Either an alien who has fled from a country because of persecution or fear of persecution due to race, religion, or political opinion, or an alien who has been displaced due to a natural disaster.

Regular Housing - Includes all housing types except conventional public housing and deep subsidy housing.

Rental Housing - a housing unit occupied by an assistance group in return for a fixed payment greater than zero that is agreed upon, either in writing or verbally, regardless of whether the unit is occupied by the person to whom the rent is paid, as long as the assistance group is not receiving government rental subsidies.

Resident - An individual who lives in the state voluntarily in a verified place of residence and who intends to remain and make their home in New Hampshire.

Resources - Assets or possessions which an individual owns. Examples of resources are cash, bank accounts, stocks, bonds, vehicles, or real estate.

Revocable Trust - A trust which can be revoked by the grantor, including trusts that are called irrevocable but which will terminate if some action is taken by the grantor.

Roomer - An individual residing with others and paying reasonable compensation to others for lodging, but not for meals.

Rooming Arrangement - The amount paid for furnished lodging excluding meals when residing in a rooming house or hotel, relative ' s home, or another person ' s home.

Roth Individual Retirement Account - A trust or a custodial account that meets most of the requirements of a Traditional Individual Retirement Account. Unlike a Traditional Individual Retirement Account:

. most contributions to the account are not tax-exempt;

. most disbursements from the account are tax-exempt;

. contributions can be made to a Roth after an individual reaches age 70 �; and

. an individual can leave funds in a Roth as long as they live.
